item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Mostly agree with SpookPizza on this. Tough I'm not against personnel eventually consuming items after they are cleaned by some tests, overall tests on this item are wildly careless, far beyond what I would expect from anything resembling a research team.

There is no safeguards whatsoever. Researchers eat unknown items without a second thought instead of calling on D-Classes. The safeguards are so good that one is injured simply because it was looking too close to a bag that boils water. And finally they get people dead because no-one thought that this thing could eventually dispense something dangerous. And it wasn't even all that dangerous, but react poorly and exploded. Even minor safeguards could have prevented such disaster.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
An interesting idea for sure, but it bugs me that any personnel would
1. Be allowed to consume vended items
and
2. That any professor would volunteer to eat aliens with little to no information as to their origin and composition. Feeling very LOLFoundation-y.

I feel like outside of testing on D-Class personnel, the Foundation would simply record and contain vended items, to either be used for later testing or just to have a record of the items dispensed. The Foundation going "As long as the SH&S guys say it's safe, snack away!" is entirely out of character, at least in my eyes.

Other than that, it's a decently interesting skip.

Good job to those who worked on the experiment logs. I am saddened that I'll never get to try half these snacks, and horrified by much the remainder.

item.title: Love this SCP
item.content:encoded:
A prime example of a well-made SCP. It tells a story without literally telling a story. It's simple, and it's "a thing that does a thing," which makes for a far more interesting SCP than the Series III SCPs that are mostly abstract concepts rather than concrete anomalous objects.

I especially like the weird, alien products that it dispenses. Those pyramids sound like they're some kind of military or travel rations, and the little creatures in the box sound like they're some kind of alien delicacy considered best when cooked live similar to lobster.

So here we have the infamous vending machine article, one that has a knack for spitting out weird canned drinks. Turns out we have an article that is a weird canned drink in SCP-2107. A seamless link, it would seem, would be if SCP-261 vended a can of SCP-2017. I am recommending the following addition be included in the articles base testing section, after lemon clams, but before the first unknown:

"Diet Ghost" - A can containing an instance of SCP-2107. Packaging was in English. Testing done on this instance provided similar results to other contained instances of SCP-2107. This marks the first time SCP-261 has vended another SCP object.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.content:encoded:
The coffee machine pulls things from our reality, which causes its effects to potentially breach containment, particularly with vague inputs. It's pretty obvious why it's Euclid.

The vending machine is pulling things from elsewhere and while the snacks it vends could have potentially dangerous effects, using the machine itself is perfectly safe.

I'd say it's a fine line and it may straddle it.

(This is my personal opinion, no idea if an "official" answer exists)
